runtime_policy_notes: The generic delta_t surface preserves admitted totals on each source product's published basis; it does not ambiently retarget HPIERS DE430/LE430 totals to DE441.

The generic delta_t surface uses an explicit 100-year C0 reconciliation from the earlier polynomial at -2100 to the first HPIERS row at -2000; the source-bounded physical surface still begins at -2000.
The HPIERS HTML DATE display rounds 1950-2016 half-year samples to integers; the packaged artifact restores the authority-declared 0.5-year ordinal cadence before interpolation.

USNO annual and Jan-Apr 2026 aggregate means are materialized at the mean epoch of their first-of-month source samples, not at integer product labels; the bridge/aggregate uncertainty scale is 0.06 seconds and is not a calibrated probability statement.
The final Delta-T aggregate is a Jan-Apr 2026 partial mean; the slope from the final two representative sample epochs is provisional aggregate policy, not an observed instantaneous derivative.
Hybrid and physical JD transforms use an exact private fraction-of-calendar-year coordinate; the public NASA-compatible decimal-year helper retains its month-midpoint convention.
Computational representability guards are +/-100000 decimal years and +/-40000000 Julian days; these are not scientific-validity or source-coverage claims.

Rows are admitted for runtime use under the packaged snapshot policy, but must not all be described as measured or definitive observations.
At each outer coverage edge, the difference from the year model tapers to zero over one Julian year; internal gaps reconcile only their admitted boundary values.
Private UT1-to-UTC display conversion inverts the within-day UT1-TAI relation so a positive UTC leap is not smeared across the preceding civil day.

units.epoch: decimal_year; exact half-year cadence from 1950 through 2016

caveats: The authority states that 1950-2016 values are half-yearly; the HTML DATE display rounds those labels to integers, so the packaged artifact restores the declared cadence rather than collapsing distinct epochs.
Exact duplicate rows are inert. At the conflicting published epochs -1600 and 1850, Moira explicitly retains the later row; -1600 is compatibility policy, while 1850 is a precision/regime join.

The HPIERS source states that its tabulated means are tied to JPL DE430/LE430 and lunar tidal acceleration -25.85 arcsec/cy^2; generic delta_t preserves that source basis and performs no ambient DE441 retargeting.
Generic delta_t joins the earlier polynomial to the first packaged HPIERS row with an explicit 100-year C0 bridge from -2100 to -2000.
The physical-policy domain begins at the first packaged epoch and does not clamp earlier requests.
